candidate: Chrono Divide (proprietary) ecosystem: chronodivide.com client, chronodivide/mod-sdk, @chronodivide/game-api, RA2WEB deploy packs (ra2web/ra2web.github.io, webra2/webra2.github.io), shuowang-ai/ra2web-chronodivide-bot, ammaarreshi/RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad
summary:
Chrono Divide (CD) is the most faithful and most active browser RA2 today. It is a from-scratch TypeScript engine by Alexandru Ciucă. Client v0.84.0 shipped on 3 Sep 2026, and releases came out roughly monthly through 2026. It is also closed source with no license. The Terms of Service keep all rights with the site operator. The mod-sdk repo has no LICENSE, and both the game-api package and the playground are "UNLICENSED".

What the official client does well: vanilla RA2 online multiplayer (quick match, ladder, 2v2, up to 8 players plus an observer), skirmish against an AI bot (Supalosa's bot, Easy/Medium/Brutal), replays, and INI/MIX mods.

What it lacks: no Allied or Soviet campaign (there is no campaign screen or module in the v0.84 bundle), no playable Yuri's Revenge, no save/load, no in-game FMV, no LAN, and no map editor.

The mod SDK only lets you change data: rules/art/sound INI, and SHP/VXL/TMP/PAL files at the original 8-bit palette and pixel scale inside expand##/ecache##.mix. You cannot change shaders or the renderer. Particles/ParticleSystems and HVA animation are unsupported.

The compiled client is minified but not obfuscated. It keeps its 1,257 SystemJS module names (e.g. engine/gfx/Renderer, engine/gfx/material/paletteShaderLib) and its class names. It uses a global Three.js r94 on WebGL1 and never reads devicePixelRatio. Injecting post-processing at runtime is technically plausible; RA2WEB's ra2web-proxy already injects code into the CD client. Distributing such changes would need the author's permission.

The ra2web packs are derivatives of the CD client with an unclear legal status:
- RA2WEB v0.87: its own build of CD code with CD branding stripped. It adds campaign and YR code. It ships an AGPL-3.0 license that contradicts its own non-commercial clause, and it names REDHASH Co., Ltd. as copyright holder.
- webra2: a scraped mirror of CD v0.57 with no license, whose README says the history contains MIX game files.

ammaarreshi's iOS port builds on huangkaoya/ts-redalert2. That tree was reconstructed from RA2WEB's compiled client and claims GPL-3.0 while its own README credits all rights to CD's author. The iOS README itself says it exists "at Alexandru Ciucă's sufferance", which contradicts the "used with the author's permission" line in its GitHub description.

Verdict: this is the best technical base only if the author gives written permission, ideally with source access. That would probably be a paid license, but this is unverified: only a Chinese site of unknown ownership, chronodivide.cn, tells developers to "buy authorization" via Discord. Without permission it is not a legal base for an HD remaster.

provenance:
Original work. Chrono Divide is a clean-room, black-box reimplementation in TypeScript by Alexandru Ciucă (GitHub: use-strict, Romanian). All derivatives come from it:
- RA2WEB (ra2web.github.io, v0.87.0): its own build of CD-derived code.
- webra2.github.io: a scraped mirror of CD v0.57.
- huangkaoya/ts-redalert2: a TypeScript source tree reconstructed from RA2WEB's compiled client.
- ammaarreshi/RedAlert2-Mac-iOS-iPad: vendors huangkaoya @8c07f10.
- shuowang-ai/ra2web-chronodivide-bot: fork of ra2web's fork of Supalosa's bot, and only a bot.
provenance_evidence:
VERIFIED:
- CD patch notes start at v0.1 (31 Oct 2020). The PPM thread (topic-59733) opened 30 Mar 2021 by "seppuku". The mod-sdk commits are by "Alexandru Ciuca <gmail.rulz@yahoo.com>", and GitHub user use-strict is "Alexandru Ciucă".
- The official client (game.chronodivide.com, style.css?v=0.84.0) mounts into a div id "ra2web-root", so "ra2web" is CD's internal name.
- RA2WEB's js/app.js (assetVersion 0.87.0-r79e73e7) contains CD class and module identifiers (PalettePhongMaterial, ShpTextureAtlas, LightingDirector, the string "map_surface_shadow", VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder in worker.js) and zero occurrences of "chronodivide". It also has campaign code (CampaignMissionList, SovietCampaign, TutorialCampaign, continueCampaign) and YR mix loading (ra2md.mix, expandmd01.mix). Its config.json points to its own CDNs: campaignBaseUrl //res2.wangerhuoda.cn/campaign/, gameResArchiveUrl https://download.ra2web.com/full-pack.7z, and a cors proxy on game.chronodivide.com.
- The ra2web org bio says "Collaborative project with Chronodivide". ra2web.com calls itself "the mirror site for Chronodivide ... a closed-source project with its own intellectual property". I found no statement from the CD author confirming this collaboration.
- ra2web-proxy README: a gateway that forwards the official Chronodivide client and dynamically injects code.
- webra2.github.io README: auto-downloaded from game.chronodivide.com with chronodivide-downloader (a fork of antsanchez/go-download-web). Its VERSION goes up to 0.57, and the README says all MIX files are in the commit history.
- ammaarreshi README: the engine lineage is "Chrono Divide → RA2WEB → huangkaoya/redalert2 @ 8c07f10". huangkaoya's README says the project was "developed based on the analysis of the Chinese version of Chronodivide — RA2WEB".
tech_stack:
VERIFIED from the downloaded client at game.chronodivide.com, v0.84.0:
- Main bundle: TypeScript compiled to SystemJS v0.19.41 System.register modules in dist/ra2web.min.js (2,439,421 bytes, 116 lines, 1,257 named modules: game 584, gui 264, engine 202, network 83, data 65).
- vendor.bundle.min.js contains React 16.13.1.
- Three.js r94 (REVISION="94") is loaded as a window global from lib/three.min.js. The index.html check requires only WebGL1, and instancing uses the ANGLE_instanced_arrays extension.
- Three add-ons: three.shader-patch.js (patches ShaderChunk for instancing), three.octree.js, SimplexNoise, LightningStrike.js, TrailRenderer.js, and shader-particle-engine (SPE) 1.0.6 plus SPE.patch.js.
- Other pieces: growingpacker (atlas packing), lzo1x, 7z WASM for archive import, ffmpeg.wasm to convert BIK video to WebM, and a virtual file system on OPFS/IndexedDB.
- Networking: client-server over WebSocket, with Cloudflare Turnstile.
- Headless engine: npm @chronodivide/game-api 0.79.0 (Node >=20, depends on three ^0.94.0, uglify-mangled).
- RA2WEB's fork now ships ES-module bundles (js/app.js, vendor.js, worker.js) and still uses Three r94.
renderer_architecture:
VERIFIED from module sources in ra2web.min.js:
- engine/gfx/Renderer creates `new THREE.WebGLRenderer({canvas, preserveDrawingBuffer:true, powerPreference:"high-performance"})` with autoClear=false, shadowMap.enabled=true, localClippingEnabled=true and toneMapping=THREE.NoToneMapping. For each scene in a Set it calls clearDepth, setViewport, then renderer.render(scene, camera).
- It recovers from webglcontextlost. There are no setPixelRatio or devicePixelRatio calls (0 occurrences).
- Cameras are THREE.OrthographicCamera; the map is a real 3D world viewed isometrically. Lighting is one DirectionalLight plus an AmbientLight, with shadows received on a ShadowMaterial "map_surface_shadow" plane (MapSurface).
- Palettes: sprites and tiles store the palette index in the texture alpha channel. paletteShaderLib samples a palette DataTexture (row = palette offset, e.g. house colours), adds extraLight, and clamps. Materials are PaletteBasicMaterial, PaletteLambertMaterial and PalettePhongMaterial.
- TMP terrain: MapTileLayer draws each TMP tile with TmpDrawable into a TextureAtlas and builds merged sprite geometry at Coords.tile3dToWorld positions, scaled by ISO_WORLD_SCALE. Per-tile lighting comes from engine/Lighting (map [Lighting] ambient, level and tint plus tile lights) as vertex colours.
- SHP sprites: ShpBuilder, SpriteBuilder, ShpTextureAtlas, BatchShpBuilder and MapSpriteBatchLayer.
- VXL voxels become real 3D meshes (VxlBuilder, VxlBatchedBuilder, and VxlGeometryMonotone/Culled/NaiveBuilder) lit by the Three.js lights. The mod-sdk confirms voxels.vpl is unsupported because the 3D engine handles voxel lighting. HVA animation is first frame only; rotors are procedural.
- Effects: engine/renderable/fx/* (LaserFx, TeslaFx, SparkFx, RadBeamFx, LineTrailFx, TrailerSmokeFx, DamageSmokeFx), engine/gfx/lighting/* (LightingDirector, NukeLightingFx, LightningStormFx) and ShipWakeTrailPlugin.
- Water is ordinary TMP tiles plus ripple animations; there is no water shader.
- Graphics options are only Model quality, Shadow quality and resolution. Camera zoom works only with the debug freeCamera console variable.

Minification: identifiers are mangled locally, but module ids (original source paths), class names and properties are kept. There are no source maps and no string-array obfuscation (0 matches for _0x patterns). The main site gives no indication of WebGPU or WebGL2 use.

build_result:
There is no engine source, so the engine itself cannot be built.
- chronodivide/mod-sdk (cloned to scratchpad/repos/chronodivide__mod-sdk) is documentation plus 7 INI files, with nothing to build.
- chronodivide/game-api-playground: with the dependency bumped to @chronodivide/game-api@0.79.0, `npm install --ignore-scripts` succeeded on Node v26.0.0 (31 packages).
  - `tsc -p .` wrote dist/exampleBot.js but reported 1 error: TS2322, "'serverUrl' does not exist in type 'CreateOnlineOpts'". This comes from the breaking API change in game-api 0.78.
  - `import('@chronodivide/game-api')` works and exposes 53 exports.
  - `node .` fails in cdapi.init → Engine.initVfs because no RA2 MIX files exist on this machine (expected).
- The browser client was not run because no game files are present. Its bundles were downloaded for static inspection only, into scratchpad/cd_site/game.
feature_completeness:
Official CD v0.84 against the checklist. [C] = verified in client code or mod-sdk, [N] = patch notes, [P] = press.

- Allied campaign: NO. The ScreenType enum has Home, Skirmish, QuickGame, CustomGame, Lobby, Replay… and no Campaign; "campaign" appears 0 times in ra2web.min.js [C]. MAPS.md (engine 0.70) marks Win, Lose, Reinforcement, CreateTeam, PlayMovie, AllowWin and others unsupported [C]. heise says it is under development [P].
- Soviet campaign: NO (same evidence).
- Yuri's Revenge: NO playable YR. EngineType.YurisRevenge and md-mix loading scaffolding exist [C]. README says "Yuri's Revenge mods are NOT compatible", and the author's issue replies say vanilla only [C].
- Skirmish vs AI: YES. The Supalosa bot has been built in since v0.57 (Jan 2024) [N], with AiDifficulty Easy/Medium/Brutal [C]. The retail ai.ini, [AI], [IQ] and difficulty INI settings are unsupported (RULES.md) [C]. The ammaarreshi README documents weak stock-bot behaviour.
- Online multiplayer: YES. Client-server over WebSocket with quick match, ladder, 2v2 parties, and 8 players plus an observer [N].
- LAN: NO (no LAN or WebRTC code [C]).
- Units, buildings and superweapons: vanilla RA2 roster largely YES [N][C] (e.g. ChronoSphereEffect, IronCurtainEffect, LightningStormEffect, NukeEffect). Partial: Particles/ParticleSystems unsupported, HVA first frame only, some art/rules keys unsupported [C].
- Naval and water: YES (ship wake, sinking, water clipping) [C][N].
- Bridges: YES [N][C].
- Garrisoning: YES [N].
- Veterancy: YES [N].
- Chronosphere, Iron Curtain and specials: YES [C].
- Shroud: YES. The FogOfWar map special flag is unsupported [C].
- Custom maps: .map and .mpr YES; .yrm NO [C].
- Sound, EVA and music: YES [C]. Music is converted to MP3, and theme.ini is not customizable [C].
- FMV: NO in-game. Only the menu BIK is converted to WebM via ffmpeg.wasm; [Movies] and PlayMovie are unsupported [C].
- Save/load: NO (no module [C]).
- Replays: YES, including server replays and per-player perspective [N][C].
- INI modding: YES for rules/art/sound INI and MIX overrides, with detailed support tables [C].
- Map editor: NO [C].
- High-resolution performance: fast (batched sprites, instancing), but WebGL1/r94. With no devicePixelRatio handling, a Retina Mac almost certainly renders at CSS-pixel resolution and upscales (inference from code). The ammaarreshi fork had to add DPR rendering. Resolution options are limited, zoom is debug-only, and there is a low-graphics preset for mobile [C].

Derivatives, claimed in their READMEs or visible in code strings and not run by me:
- RA2WEB v0.87: campaign UI and resource download, YR mixes [C strings].
- ammaarreshi: playable YR, replay-based save/load, stronger AI, DPR rendering [README].
asset_requirements: You need original RA2 game files: ra2.mix, language.mix, multi.mix, theme.mix and the rest, plus the md*.mix files for any YR attempt. They are imported into the browser's sandboxed VFS (OPFS/IndexedDB); music is converted to MP3 and the menu BIK to WebM. CD itself distributes no EA assets, but its import flow offers an Internet Archive download (webra2's mirrored config shows archive.org Red-Alert-2-Multiplayer.exe, and heise mentions the IA link). The headless game-api needs MIX_DIR pointing at a retail install. The Steam C&C Ultimate Collection RA2/YR (app 2229850) is the clean legal source. The RA2WEB pack's config points at its own full-pack.7z and campaign resource CDNs, which likely redistribute EA files; that is an inference and I did not download them. webra2's README says MIX files are in its git history. Neither is an acceptable asset source.
hd_extensibility:
With the mod SDK only (sanctioned):
- You can override SHP, VXL, TMP and PAL files through expand##/ecache##.mix, and INI data through rules/art/soundcd-style merging.
- You cannot ship true HD 2D art. The pipeline stores an 8-bit palette index in the texture alpha channel (paletteShaderLib) and places sprites at native pixel size (SpriteUtils with ISO_WORLD_SCALE). There is no art.ini scale key and no PNG sprite path; glsl.png is only the splash screen.
- Denser VXL models might render finer because voxels become meshes (inference, untested), but colours stay palette-bound.
- Nothing in the SDK touches shaders, post-processing, water, weather or particles, and [Particles]/[ParticleSystems] are unsupported.

Runtime injection (technically plausible, legally needs permission to distribute):
- THREE r94 is a global loaded before the bundle, and the bundle maps "three" to window.THREE.
- The engine's own lib/three/three.shader-patch.js shows that ShaderChunk patching at load time works.
- Named SystemJS modules can in principle be fetched at runtime (e.g. SystemJS.import("engine/gfx/Renderer")) and their prototypes monkeypatched. This is standard SystemJS behaviour, not tested here.
- RA2WEB's ra2web-proxy already does proxy-side code injection into the CD client.

Hook points in the client (module ids, VERIFIED to exist):
- engine/gfx/Renderer: add a WebGLRenderTarget plus EffectComposer passes (bloom, ACES tonemapping, colour grading, SMAA/FXAA, sharpening) and setPixelRatio(devicePixelRatio) for Retina.
- engine/gfx/material/paletteShaderLib, PaletteBasicMaterial, PalettePhongMaterial, PaletteLambertMaterial: an RGBA/HD texture path and normal-map lighting would need a new material branch here.
- engine/renderable/entity/map/MapTileLayer and MapSurface: water and terrain shaders. Water tiles would have to be detected by tile type or land type.
- engine/renderable/builder/ShpBuilder, ShpTextureAtlas, SpriteBuilder, BatchShpBuilder: replace atlases with upscaled RGBA art.
- engine/renderable/builder/VxlBuilder and vxlGeometry/*: voxel-to-mesh already exists; swap in smoothed or PBR meshes.
- engine/gfx/lighting/LightingDirector, LightingFx, LightningStormFx, NukeLightingFx, and engine/Lighting: weather and time-of-day.
- engine/renderable/fx/* (LaserFx, TeslaFx, SparkFx, DamageSmokeFx…) and handler/WarheadDetonateFxHandler: modern hit and explosion effects, e.g. with the bundled SPE particle engine.

Constraints: WebGL1 and a 2018 Three.js with no WebGL2, MRT or WebGPU. Hooks break on every roughly monthly client update. Online play could flag a modified client. A proper HD remaster (RGBA atlases, depth/normal buffers, WebGL2/WebGPU upgrade) realistically needs engine source access from the author.
risks: Hard legal blocker: the engine is proprietary. The ToS reserves all IP, the mod-sdk has no license, and game-api is UNLICENSED. Modifying or redistributing the client for an HD remaster needs Alexandru Ciucă's written permission, possibly paid (the chronodivide.cn claim is unverified), and that permission has not been obtained.
No engine source is available. Renderer changes are only possible through brittle runtime monkeypatching of a minified bundle that is released about monthly.

The derivative chain is legally unsound: RA2WEB's AGPL-3.0 conflicts with its own non-commercial/REDHASH clause and has no documented grant from CD; webra2 is a scraped mirror with MIX files in its history; huangkaoya's GPL-3.0 claim is contradicted by its own README; ammaarreshi's 'used with the author's permission' description is contradicted by its README ('at Alexandru Ciucă's sufferance'). Building on any of them inherits takedown risk.

Big missing features in the official client: no campaigns, no playable YR, no save/load, no FMV, no LAN, no map editor. Campaign trigger actions (Win, Lose, Reinforcement, CreateTeam, PlayMovie, etc.) are listed as unsupported.

The mod SDK cannot deliver HD: art is an 8-bit palette index in the texture alpha at native pixel scale; there are no shader or post-process hooks; Particles/ParticleSystems and HVA animation are unsupported.

Old renderer: Three.js r94 on WebGL1 with no devicePixelRatio handling, so it is almost certainly blurry on the user's 3456x2234 Retina display. Getting to 2026-level effects needs a renderer overhaul that only the source owner can do properly.
A modified client used online may breach ToS or be treated as cheating (Cloudflare Turnstile, ladder integrity). Render-only hooks are unlikely to desync the simulation, but that is inference.
Bus factor of 1: a single author controls the engine, servers and accounts.
The in-game skirmish AI (Supalosa bot and forks) is UNLICENSED.
Asset legality: CD links to an Internet Archive installer, and the RA2WEB packs point at their own full game-resource archives and campaign CDNs. Use the user's own Steam or retail copy only.
score_rationale:
On technical fidelity alone, CD would score about 8. It has the most faithful deterministic RA2 simulation, active monthly development through Sep 2026, a strong multiplayer and replay stack, an introspectable module structure, and voxels that are already 3D meshes. The brief makes legal permission a hard constraint, and none exists: the engine is proprietary with no license, the ToS reserves all rights, and every source-bearing derivative (RA2WEB, huangkaoya, ammaarreshi) has an unverified or contradictory licensing chain.

It is also a poor fit even for step 1 without source access. Campaigns, YR, save/load and FMV are all missing from the official client. For step 2, the sanctioned mod SDK cannot change the renderer or add HD art, and an HD remaster through runtime injection into a closed, frequently updated client would be fragile and could not be distributed without permission.

The score is 3 rather than 0–1 because a realistic path exists. The author is reachable (contact@chronodivide.com, the Discord, GitHub @use-strict) and has granted small permissions quickly before (mod-sdk issue #7). If he grants written permission plus source access, this rises to about 8. Until then, treat CD as a reference implementation and possible partner. Do not use it, or any ra2web or huangkaoya derivative, as the code base.
